featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Revolution
featured_videos.editorial_title: 3 Carnivore Mistakes That Made Me Feel Worse!
featured_videos.commentary: The "worse before better" thing is so real, and I think this video nails why so many people bail too early. Most of the community comments here are pointing to the same culprit: salt and electrolytes. That person who went from 150mmHg blood pressure down to normal just by adding salt? That's not a coincidence. A lot of people start carnivore expecting their body to feel amazing immediately, but they're actually walking into a dehydration and electrolyte deficit without realizing it. Check out our electrolyte guide if you're dealing with fatigue or weird symptoms in week two. The other thing I'm noticing in these comments is patience, which honestly sounds like something we don't talk about enough. Your body isn't broken if it takes a month to adjust. Stick with it.

featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Claire
featured_videos.editorial_title: 6 Carnivore Habits That Destroy Love Handles & Make You Richer (140lbs Lost)
featured_videos.commentary: Claire nails something I see over and over in coaching: the people who stick with carnivore long-term aren't the ones obsessing over perfection, they're the ones who solve the practical problems first. Budget stress and meal boredom kill more diets than any macro miscalculation ever will. The crockpot cube steak trick, shopping on a full stomach, buying in bulk at Costco. these aren't sexy hacks, but they're exactly what makes the difference between "I tried carnivore for three weeks" and "I lost 140 pounds." When you remove friction from the diet, you remove the excuses that derail you. That's when real change happens.

featured_videos.editorial_title: Is Culver's the Best Carnivore Fast Food?
featured_videos.commentary: The real takeaway here isn't about Culver's pricing or even the a la carte hack, though that $1.90 patty thing is solid for budget-conscious people. It's that one comment hitting hard: "Ordering simple meat should not feel like a puzzle." That's the whole problem right there. You'd think asking for plain beef patties would be straightforward, but instead people are getting pushback, confusion, or regional inconsistencies (looking at you, Scottsdale). From my experience coaching, this friction alone causes people to give up on eating out. they just drive home and cook instead. The good news? HomeSteadHow is mapping these places out so you don't waste time or money. If you're eating carnivore and want to know what actually works at chain restaurants, this kind of on-the-ground intel beats guessing every time.

featured_videos.title: You Ate ZERO Carbs… Why Is Your Blood Sugar Rising?
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: You Ate ZERO Carbs… Why Is Your Blood Sugar Rising?
featured_videos.commentary: Okay, this is the dawn phenomenon question that shows up in my coaching inbox at least once a week, usually from someone panicking at their CGM data. Dr. Hampton's explaining gluconeogenesis, but what I love about the comments here is that people are *getting it* now, not just the theory but how it actually plays out. Someone mentioned they know their body well enough to predict it, and that's the real skill, right? That's what happens when you stop fighting the process and start understanding your own metabolic rhythm. The fasting comments show people learning through their own data too, not just blindly trusting a number on the screen. This matters because so many people quit carnivore thinking their blood sugar control broke, when really it's just their liver doing exactly what it's supposed to do. If you're seeing elevated fasting glucose on carnivore, check out our CGM guide, it covers this exact scenario and why timing matters more than panic.
